author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That it is sweet to despise the world and to serve God

verses.text: Now will I speak again, O my Lord, and hold not my peace; I will say in the ears of my God, my Lord, and my King, who is exalted above all, Oh how plentiful is Thy goodness which Thou hast laid up for them that fear Thee!(1) But what art Thou to those who love Thee?
verses.modernizedText: Now I will speak again, O my Lord, and not be silent; I will say in the ears of my God, my Lord, and my King, who is exalted above all, Oh how plentiful is Your goodness which You have laid up for those who fear You!(1) But what are You to those who love You?

verses.text: What to those who serve Thee with their whole heart?
verses.modernizedText: What are You to those who serve You with their whole heart?

verses.text: Truly unspeakable is the sweetness of the contemplation of Thee, which Thou bestowest upon those who love Thee.
verses.modernizedText: Truly unspeakable is the sweetness of the contemplation of You, which You bestow upon those who love You.

verses.text: In this most of all Thou hast showed me the sweetness of Thy charity, that when I was not, Thou madest me, and when I wandered far from Thee, Thou broughtest me back that I might serve Thee, and commandedst me to love Thee.
verses.modernizedText: In this above all You have shown me the sweetness of Your charity, that when I was not, You made me, and when I wandered far from You, You brought me back that I might serve You, and commanded me to love You.

verses.text: O Fountain of perpetual love, what shall I say concerning Thee?
verses.modernizedText: O Fountain of perpetual love, what shall I say concerning You?

verses.text: How shall I be unmindful of Thee, who didst vouchsafe to remember me, even after I pined away and perished?
verses.modernizedText: How shall I forget You, who were pleased to remember me, even after I pined away and perished?

verses.text: Thou hast had mercy beyond all hope upon Thy servant, and hast showed Thy grace and friendship beyond all deserving.
verses.modernizedText: You have had mercy beyond all hope upon Your servant, and have shown Your grace and friendship beyond all deserving.

verses.text: What reward shall I render Thee for this Thy grace?
verses.modernizedText: What reward shall I give You for this Your grace?

verses.text: For it is not given unto all to renounce this world and its affairs, and to take up a religious life.
verses.modernizedText: For it is not given to all to renounce this world and its affairs, and to take up a religious life.

verses.text: For is it a great thing that I should serve Thee, whom every creature ought to serve?
verses.modernizedText: For is it a great thing that I should serve You, whom every creature ought to serve?

verses.text: It ought not to seem a great thing to me to serve Thee; but rather this appeareth to me a great and wonderful thing, that Thou vouchsafest to receive as Thy servant one so poor and unworthy, and to join him unto Thy chosen servants.
verses.modernizedText: It ought not to seem a great thing to me to serve You; but rather this appears to me a great and wonderful thing, that You are pleased to receive as Your servant one so poor and unworthy, and to join him to Your chosen servants.

verses.text: Behold all things which I have are Thine, and with them I serve Thee.
verses.modernizedText: Behold, all things which I have are Yours, and with them I serve You.

verses.text: And yet verily it is Thou who servest me, rather than I Thee.
verses.modernizedText: And yet truly it is You who serve me, rather than I You.

verses.text: Behold the heaven and the earth which Thou hast created for the service of men; they are at Thy bidding, and perform daily whatsoever Thou dost command.
verses.modernizedText: Behold the heaven and the earth which You have created for the service of men; they are at Your command, and perform daily whatever You command.

verses.text: Yea, and this is little; for Thou hast even ordained the Angels for the service of man.
verses.modernizedText: Yes, and this is little; for You have even ordained the Angels for the service of man.

verses.text: But it surpasseth even all these things, that Thou Thyself didst vouchsafe to minister unto man, and didst promise that Thou wouldest give Thyself unto him.
verses.modernizedText: But it surpasses even all these things, that You Yourself were pleased to minister to man, and promised that You would give Yourself to him.

verses.text: What shall I render unto Thee for all these Thy manifold mercies?
verses.modernizedText: What shall I give You for all these Your manifold mercies?

verses.text: Oh that I were able to serve Thee all the days of my life!
verses.modernizedText: Oh that I were able to serve You all the days of my life!

verses.text: Oh that even for one day I were enabled to do Thee service worthy of Thyself!
verses.modernizedText: Oh that even for one day I were enabled to do You service worthy of Yourself!

verses.text: For verily Thou art worthy of all service, all honour, and praise without end.
verses.modernizedText: For truly You are worthy of all service, all honor, and praise without end.

verses.text: Verily Thou art my God, and I am Thy poor servant, who am bound to serve Thee with all my strength, nor ought I ever to grow weary of Thy praise.
verses.modernizedText: Truly You are my God, and I am Your poor servant, who am bound to serve You with all my strength, nor ought I ever to grow weary of Your praise.

verses.text: This is my wish, this is my exceeding great desire, and whatsoever is lacking to me, vouchsafe Thou to supply.
verses.modernizedText: This is my wish, this is my exceedingly great desire, and whatever is lacking to me, be pleased to supply.

verses.text: It is great honour, great glory to serve Thee, and to despise all for Thy sake.
verses.modernizedText: It is great honor, great glory to serve You, and to despise all for Your sake.

verses.text: For they shall have great grace who of their own will shall submit themselves to Thy most holy service.
verses.modernizedText: For they will have great grace who of their own will submit themselves to Your most holy service.

verses.text: They who for Thy love have cast away every carnal delight shall find the sweetest consolation of the Holy Ghost.
verses.modernizedText: Those who for Your love have cast away every carnal delight will find the sweetest consolation of the Holy Ghost.

verses.text: They who enter the narrow way of life for Thy Name’s sake, and have put away all worldly cares, shall attain great liberty of spirit.
verses.modernizedText: Those who enter the narrow way of life for Your Name’s sake, and have put away all worldly cares, will attain great liberty of spirit.

verses.text: Oh grateful and delightsome service of God, whereby man is made truly free and holy!
verses.modernizedText: Oh grateful and delightful service of God, by which man is made truly free and holy!

verses.text: Oh sacred condition of the religious servant, which maketh man equal to the Angels, well-pleasing unto God, terrible to evil spirits, and acceptable to all faithful ones!
verses.modernizedText: Oh sacred condition of the religious servant, which makes man equal to the Angels, well pleasing to God, terrible to evil spirits, and acceptable to all faithful ones!

verses.text: Oh service to be embraced and ever desired, in which the highest good is promised, and joy is gained which shall remain for evermore!
verses.modernizedText: Oh service to be embraced and ever desired, in which the highest good is promised, and joy is gained which will remain forevermore!
